newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Three groups seen bidding on Brazil's CRT shares.
newsitem.headline: Three groups seen bidding on Brazil's CRT shares.

text.p: Three foreign-led groups are expected to bid today on a 35-percent stake in Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) despite court complaints lodged against the sale, a state official said.
"At this point, it's still scheduled to take place," a spokeswoman for Rio Grande do Sul state, which owns the firm, told Reuters.
Three lawsuits seeking to halt the auction were tossed out by judges on Monday and another five were dismissed this morning, leaving one to be ruled on before the auction, she said.

The complaints, which came in the last several days, were filed by a local newspaper, a radio station, a group of state lawmakers, city councilmen, the CRT workers union and others opposed to the auction.
"It looks like the auction will take place because they're all the same complaint," the spokeswoman said.
The suits complained that the state, as a result of the sale and transfer of a separate three percent stake to workers, would lose control of CRT.
Rio Grande do Sul officials said that, in the end, the state would be left with a 51 percent controlling interest.

The state has set a base price of 440 million reais ($423.5 million) for 35 percent of CRT's capital stock, or 262,352,653 voting shares. The auction is slated for 1100 local/1300 GMT/0800 EST at Rio Grande do Sul's capital of Porto Alegre.
The CRT shares sale is being closely watched by the market because it kicks off the privatisation of Brazil's telecoms sector, including federally owned giant Telebras.
"This will give the market an idea of what foreign investors are willing to pay for a Brazilian telecom. It will serve as a valuation benchmark," one analyst said.
Of six consortia originally prequalified for the bidding, three dropped out last week. The groups still expected to bid are:
* France Telecom with locals Banco Opportunity, Banco do Brasil and pension funds Previ, Sistel, CRT Employees Fund and Telos.
* Italy's STET and Argentina's Perez Companc S.A. with locals Camargo Correa and Bradesco .
* Telefonica Internacional de Espana of Spain with Brazil's RBS Participacoes S.A. and Cia de Telecomunicaciones de Chile, Telefonica de Argentina and Citicorp.
Consortia led by Korea Telekom, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Co and GTE Corp's GTE International Telecommunications Inc pulled out earlier this month without citing reasons.
However, the six groups prequalified before the state set its base price for the shares or published bid specifications.
